title: Log Lineage and Versioning Playbook v0.1
content:
Purpose:
This playbook captures a pragmatic approach for evolving Redwood's audit/event surface: how we name events, attach lineage and evidence, and version schema changes in a way that preserves downstream SIEM exports, preserves RBAC v2 intent, and enables evidence automation. It is intended for security engineers, SREs, platform and product owners who emit or consume audit events.

Scope and goals:
- Define a consistent event identity and lineage model that lets consumers map events across versions and model variants.
- Propose a versioning policy that balances agility with backwards compatibility for SIEM and analytics consumers.
- Document RBAC v2 relevant fields and how role changes should be recorded in the audit trail.
- Provide minimal transformation rules for SIEM export and evidence automation hooks (artifact references, checksum, retention tags).
- Define a migration plan from existing v1/v2 artifacts to the new harmonized approach.

High-level model: event as an immutable observation
- Each emitted record is an observation of an action at a point in time. Records are immutable and append-only.
- Canonical fields (always present): event_id, event_type, event_version, timestamp_utc, subject, actor_id, actor_type, outcome, source_service, correlation_id, lineage_ids, evidence_refs.
- Optional contextual fields: request_params, response_summary, policy_snapshot, token_context, client_ip, geo_info.

Identity and taxonomy
- event_type: short dot-delimited namespace: <domain>.<resource>.<action>. Example: auth.user.token.create or rtx.model.deploy.start. Use lower-case, hyphen-safe tokens.
- display_name: human-friendly string for dashboards.
- canonical_id: stable event identifier (GUID) that persists across renames; used for mapping historical versions. Not required in SIEM exports but stored in primary audit store.

Versioning policy (semantic-lite)
- event_version: MAJOR.MINOR where MAJOR increments on incompatible schema changes, MINOR increments on additive, backwards-compatible changes. Patch-level changes are not recorded in event_version; they live in the emission metadata.
- Backwards compatibility guarantees:
  - MINOR increases must not remove required fields or change the semantic meaning of existing fields. Consumers must continue to parse old fields.
  - MAJOR increases mean consumers must consult a transformation mapping; both versions should be emitted concurrently during a transition window.
- Transition window: default 90 days where producing service emits both old and new event_version (dual-write) and a migration job ingests both.

Field-level stability and deprecation annotations
- Schema fields should be annotated with stability tags in the registry: stable | experimental | deprecated | removed. Those annotations are carried in the schema registry metadata (not in each event).
- Deprecation lifecycle: announce -> deprecation_period (>= 90 days) -> removal in next MAJOR.

RBAC v2 considerations
- Required RBAC audit fields:
  - actor_id: unique id for the principal (user/service account).
  - actor_type: user | service | system | delegated.
  - actor_roles: list of role ids effective for the request (snapshot of RBAC v2 decision).
  - decision_context: "ALLOW" | "DENY" plus rule_id that triggered decision (if available).
- When role changes happen (role created/updated/deleted) emit a configuration event under admin.role.change with policy_snapshot containing the role definition hash and a link to the role artifact. This ensures policy drift is auditable.

Lineage and correlation
- correlation_id: consumer-facing request id that ties distributed traces; best-effort.
- lineage_ids: ordered list of event_ids showing causal chain where events transform or fork (e.g., workflow.start -> task.spawn -> worker.exec). Lineage is append-only and can be truncated for space.
- canonicalization rules: when a producing service aggregates multiple internal events into a single top-level audit record for storage/analytics, it must attach references to the original sub-event_ids in lineage_ids.

Evidence automation hooks
- evidence_refs: list of evidence objects (in the event body) with minimal fields: {"artifact_uri", "artifact_type", "sha256", "stored_at"}. For this playbook we recommend storing only references in the event and keeping artifacts in the evidence store.
- Evidence store link format: redwood-evidence://<bucket>/<path>#<sha256>. If evidence is ephemeral, include ttl_seconds in evidence metadata.
- Automation workflows should be able to query by artifact SHA256 and by event_id to rebuild case material.

SIEM export considerations
- SIEM consumers prefer flat records and stable field names. Define an export transform layer that:
  1) flattens nested structures (e.g., actor.id -> actor_id),
  2) maps arrays into comma-separated strings for indexed SIEMs,
  3) emits a minimal set of guarantee fields (event_id, event_time, event_type, actor_id, actor_ip, outcome, source_service, event_version, canonical_id).
- Tagging for SIEM: include export_tags array with values used to route/ingest into different SIEM indexes (e.g., pci, gdpr, infra, ops).
- Retention note: SIEM indices are separate and may have different retention. Make sure events include retention_class to drive downstream index lifecycle.

Compatibility and migration plan (v1 -> v2 -> v3 harmonization)
- Phase 0: Audit registry and canonical_id backfill. Run a job to assign canonical_id to historical events when predictable mapping exists (by event_type + stable key).
- Phase 1: Publish event taxonomy registry and require new producers to adopt dot-namespace event_type.
- Phase 2: Introduce event_version and evidence_refs to producers (MINOR bump). For 90 days support dual-write: emit v1 and v2 variants.
- Phase 3: Add RBAC snapshot fields as required for admin/security events (MINOR).
- Phase 4: Major release: remove obsolete fields, require canonical_id, and collapse dual-write.

Testing and validation
- Unit tests for producer libraries to validate required fields and version tag generation.
- Integration tests: consume events via the ingestion pipeline and assert flattening/transformation rules for SIEM export.
- Back-compat smoke tests: Query older indices and validate mapping to canonical_id.

Operational play for schema breakage
- If a producer accidentally emits a MAJOR incompatible change without dual-write: ingestion should route those events into a quarantine topic and alert SEC/infra channel.
- Quarantine workflow: triage -> optionally run a schema migration job to backfill missing fields -> re-insert if safe.

Example event (v1 -> v2 dual write example):
- v1 (existing):
{
  "event_id": "evt-20250915-0001",
  "event_type": "auth.token.create",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-09-15T18:02:12Z",
  "actor_id": "user:1234",
  "actor_ip": "1.2.3.4",
  "outcome": "SUCCESS"
}

- v2 (new):
{
  "event_id": "evt-20250915-0001-v2",
  "canonical_id": "c-9b8c7d6e-0001",
  "event_type": "auth.user.token.create",
  "event_version": "1.0",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-09-15T18:02:12Z",
  "actor": { "id": "user:1234", "type": "user", "roles": ["role:developer"] },
  "actor_ip": "1.2.3.4",
  "outcome": "SUCCESS",
  "evidence_refs": [ { "artifact_uri": "redwood-evidence://evidence-bucket/tokens/token-1234.json#sha256:abcd...", "artifact_type": "token-manifest", "sha256": "abcd...", "stored_at": "2025-09-15T18:02:12Z" } ]
}

(Above JSON blobs are illustrative and should be emitted as a single-line JSON in the actual event transport; here they are pretty-printed for readability.)

Rollout and stakeholders
- Owners: security-infra (schema registry & ingestion), serving-runtime (producer lib changes), platform-observability (SIEM exports), product-hosted-api (producer adoption).
- Stakeholder sync cadence: weekly during transition windows, biweekly for ongoing maintenance.

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Do we include role definitions inline in every request (actor_roles snapshot) or reference by role_hash + authoritative link? Tradeoffs: inline improves forensic completeness; references reduce per-event size. Proposed: include role_hash (required) and include inline role_defs only for admin-level events or on explicit audit-level=true requests.
- Evidence retention policy mapping between audit store and evidence store. Need legal retention classes and enforcement.
- Default transition window length for high-frequency events (>= 1M events/day) may need extension beyond 90 days to allow downstream re-indexing.

Appendix: quick checklist for a producing service owner
- [ ] Register event_type in taxonomy registry and obtain canonical_id if applicable.
- [ ] Add event_version to all emissions.
- [ ] Emit actor_roles snapshot or role_hash per RBAC v2 guidance.
- [ ] Add evidence_refs for any artifacts produced by the request.
- [ ] Validate SIEM export transform locally.
- [ ] Run dual-write for 90 days and monitor trunk metrics for missing fields.

Notes and history:
- v0.1 (2025-09-15) initial draft created by Aisha Patel.
- This playbook is intentionally pragmatic and aimed at minimizing SIEM and consumer breakage while improving forensic fidelity.
